summary: Hubert Durt was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Étienne Lamotte (~1961–1970). He was a professor at EFEO (~1970–2001) and ICPBS (~2001–2011), and directed the Hobogirin Institute (~1981).

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992–1998) under Wendy Doniger, and was appointed Associate Professor at Ohio State University around 1998.

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1924–1928). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1950), founded the Tibet Society in 1959, and was an Honorary Fellow of the British Academy.
Hugh Gray was an Indology scholar who attended Battersea Grammar School. He later served as a lecturer at SOAS, University of London, from around 1964 to 1970.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate from Stanford University (~1969–1973). He became a professor at Stony Brook University in 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

Hugo David is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012. He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of EFEO in 2015.

Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held a post at Sophia University around 1935 and studied under traditional teacher Koun Yamada (~1968–1989).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where Yi-hsun Huang served as MA supervisor.
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served as professor at Taipei National University of the Arts (~1992–2014) and president of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kuo-wei Liu.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Solonin, and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University.

Humberto Maturana was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who completed his doctorate at Harvard University (1956–1958). He was an assistant professor of biology at the University of Chile (1960) and founded Instituto Matríztica in 2000.

Hung Wu is an art historian and Sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1980–1987). He taught at Harvard before becoming the Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History at the University of Chicago in 1994.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon.

Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1940–1945). He held professorships at MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1990–2012).
Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.
Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held posts as a professor at Duke University and as a professor of religious studies at Yale University.
